keywords.def: the qualities of a letter's sound (singular sifah)
raising the back of the tongue: heavy letters
the tongue stays low: light letters
the tongue presses up like a lid: ص ض ط ظ

questions.q: Read «طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍۢ» (84:19) and name every raised letter.
questions.a: ط and ق in both words (four raised letters).

questions.q: Raised-letter hunt (pupil PDF): circle every isti'la letter in 84:16 to 25. Today's rota group recites 84:16 to 20 in turn.
Extend: write the isti'la phrase and the four itbaq letters.
questions.a: خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ; ص ض ط ظ

questions.q: Stretch: why is خ heavy but not as heavy as ط?
questions.a: خ is raised but not itbaq; ط is raised and pressed like a lid (itbaq), so it is heavier.
A) غ. غ is in خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ. ع and ه are throat letters but light.

questions.q: Think again: In Year 4 you learned heavy letters. What does the back of your tongue do on ق that it does not do on ك?
questions.a: It rises towards the roof of the mouth: isti'la (raising). That raising is what makes the letter heavy.
